I want the result to include the actual page text and a simple description of the sections and form fields, not a finished tournament announcement or an answer to players asking whether they are registered.

the event is the Cedar Quay Open, a one-day chess tournament on Saturday, September 18, 2027, at Cedar Quay Community Hall, 18 Alder Street, Port Rowan. doors open at 8:15 a.m. and the first round starts at 9:00 a.m. the schedule is five rounds using a Swiss pairing system, with a time control of 15 minutes plus a 10-second increment per move. include those details together so people don't mistake the doors-open time for the start time. the event is open to players of all ages and experience levels, and a US Chess membership is not required. don't imply that it is divided into rating or age sections; the tournament has one open section.

registration is limited to 64 players. the entry fee is $25 per player and is payable in cash at check-in; there is no online payment option. registration closes at 6:00 p.m. on Wednesday, September 15, or earlier if all 64 places are filled. if the limit is reached first, later entries should be described as a waitlist rather than confirmed seats. please make that condition visible near the registration action and don't say that submitting the form guarantees a place. players should arrive by 8:40 a.m. to check in. someone who has registered but has not checked in by 8:40 may lose their place to a waitlisted player, but only if a waitlisted player is present. phrase that carefully, since it isn't an automatic cancellation in every case.

for the form, ask for the player's full name, age, email address, and phone number. also ask whether they have a US Chess rating, and if yes, provide a box for the rating number; an unrated player should still be able to submit the form. include a field for an optional note about access needs. if a player is under 16, ask for a parent or guardian's name and contact email as well. don't make those extra fields mandatory for older players. don't ask people to enter payment card information, because the fee is paid in cash at check-in. make clear that one form is for one player, so a family registering several players should submit a separate form for each person.

we need the page to explain what happens after submission without claiming that a spot has been reserved. the organizer will email each person to confirm receipt and say whether there is an available seat or whether they are on the waitlist. the tournament contact email is chess@cedarquay.org. please show that address as the contact for questions and access requests. the page should not promise a response time that we haven't provided. there is no need to invent a phone contact for the organizer just because the registration form collects the player's phone number.

include the location and practical arrival details in a separate section. the hall is at 18 Alder Street, Port Rowan; free parking is available in the hall's rear lot, and the entrance on Alder Street has a step-free route. players may bring their own chess set and clock, but the tournament will have sets and clocks available to share, so don't present bringing equipment as compulsory. food is not provided. there is a café across the street, but it may not be open during the event, so say players should plan their own lunch rather than treating the café as a guaranteed option. don't add directions, transit information, or venue facilities we haven't listed.

there is one short quote from the organizer that i want included exactly as spoken, preferably near a welcome line: “We’re glad to have first-time players and regular tournament players at the same boards.” keep it as an ordinary welcome, not a promise about prizes or coaching. don't invent prizes, awards, cancellation terms, refunds, or a tournament director's name. If any part of the page needs to mention those topics, leave them out rather than filling in details.

maybe lay the page out in this order: 1. event name and welcome, 2. date, venue, and schedule, 3. who can enter and the fee, 4. registration form and the 64-player limit, 5. check-in and waitlist information, then 6. location and practical notes. use clear headings and compact wording, but not so compressed that the deadline and the earlier-full condition get lost. make the registration action easy to find. include a note that registration details are used to administer this event and contact the person registering, and that email addresses and phone numbers won't be shown on a public player list. keep the final page useful on its own while making it clear that a submitted form is not the same as an organizer's confirmation of a seat.
output:
Create a clear, easy-to-scan registration page for the Cedar Quay Open chess tournament within the existing website. Use the existing HTML and CSS files if you describe how the page should fit into the site; do not install packages. Provide the page copy and a simple description of its sections and form fields. Do not write a tournament announcement or respond to individual registration questions.

Organize the page with clear headings and compact wording, using this order:
1. Event name and welcome
2. Date, venue, and schedule
3. Eligibility and entry fee
4. Registration form and player limit
5. Check-in and waitlist information
6. Location and practical notes

The event is the Cedar Quay Open, a one-day tournament on Saturday, September 18, 2027, at Cedar Quay Community Hall, 18 Alder Street, Port Rowan. Doors open at 8:15 a.m.; the first round starts at 9:00 a.m. The tournament has five Swiss-system rounds with a time control of 15 minutes plus a 10-second increment per move. The event is open to players of all ages and experience levels. A US Chess membership is not required, and there is one open section, not separate rating or age sections.

The entry fee is $25 per player, payable in cash at check-in. There is no online payment option. Registration closes at 6:00 p.m. on Wednesday, September 15, or earlier if all 64 places are filled. Make the 64-player limit and the early-full condition visible near the registration action. If the limit has been reached, describe later entries as waitlisted, not as confirmed seats. Do not imply that submitting a form guarantees a place.

Ask each player for their full name, age, email address, and phone number. Ask whether they have a US Chess rating, and show a field for the rating number only if they answer yes; unrated players must still be able to submit the form. Include an optional note field for access needs. For players under 16, ask for a parent or guardian’s name and contact email; do not make these fields mandatory for older players. Do not request payment card information. State that one form is for one player and that families registering several players should submit a separate form for each person.

Do not promise a response time or claim that form submission reserves a place. Players should arrive by 8:40 a.m. to check in. A registered player who has not checked in by 8:40 may lose their place to a waitlisted player only if a waitlisted player is present; make clear that this is not an automatic cancellation in every case.

Show chess@cedarquay.org as the contact for questions and access requests. Do not invent an organizer phone number. Include a note that registration details are used to administer the event and contact the person registering, and that email addresses and phone numbers will not be shown on a public player list.

Players may bring their own chess set and clock, but the tournament will have sets and clocks available to share; do not describe personal equipment as compulsory. Food is not provided. A café across the street may not be open during the event, so advise players to plan their own lunch without presenting the café as a guaranteed option. Do not add directions, transit information, or unprovided venue facilities.

Include this organizer quote exactly as written, preferably near the welcome: “We’re glad to have first-time players and regular tournament players at the same boards.” Treat it as a welcome, not as a promise of prizes or coaching. Do not invent prizes, awards, cancellation terms, refunds, or the tournament director’s name; leave those topics out.

Keep the final page useful on its own and make clear that a submitted form is not the same as an organizer’s confirmation of a seat.

Please help me design and implement a small log-file cleanup utility for a Linux server. It will be run by an administrator from the command line and may later be scheduled, but the first version should be usable on its own. Keep the scope to selecting eligible files, reporting what would happen, and optionally deleting them. The utility should not rotate logs, compress them, or inspect their contents.

The administrator will provide a root directory and a retention period. Search that directory and its subdirectories for regular files whose names end in `.log` or `.log.N`, where `N` is one or more digits; do not treat directories or symbolic links as candidate files. Match the suffix without regard to letter case. The root directory itself must exist and be readable. If it does not, report the problem clearly and exit without deleting anything. Avoid following symbolic links while walking the tree, including a link that points back into the root, so a mistaken link cannot make the walk loop or escape the requested directory.

Treat the retention period as a positive whole number of days, supplied as an option such as `--days 30`. A file is eligible when its chosen age is at least that many days at the time the run begins. Use one captured run-start time for all comparisons in a run rather than recalculating “now” for each file. Explain which clock and timestamp fields the implementation uses, and keep comparisons consistent in the presence of time zones. A future timestamp should not make a file eligible. The administrator may also supply `--now` with an ISO-8601 timestamp for repeatable tests; if provided, validate it before walking the directory.

For ordinary files, decide age from a timestamp in the filename when it follows `service-YYYYMMDD.log` or `service-YYYYMMDD.log.N`, with any nonempty service name that contains no slash. Interpret that date in UTC. If the filename does not match this dated pattern, or its date is not a real calendar date, fall back to the file’s modification time. Make that fallback explicit in the report so the administrator can tell why a file was selected. Do not reject an otherwise eligible file merely because its name is not dated. If the modification time cannot be read, skip that file, record a useful per-file warning, and continue with other candidates.

Please make the age-selection rule easy to review. In particular, preserve this precedence: a valid date in the supported filename pattern is the age source; otherwise the file modification time is the age source. Do not use the creation time, access time, file size, or a date found somewhere else in the path. For a valid filename date, compare the start of that UTC date with the run-start time. For the fallback, compare the modification timestamp directly. State how the day threshold is calculated at the boundary, and include tests for a file exactly at the threshold and one just short of it. These details matter because an administrator may compare a report from one run with a later dry run.

Offer two modes. In dry-run mode, which should be the default, print the eligible paths and the age source used for each one, but do not remove or modify any files. In deletion mode, enabled by `--delete`, attempt to remove each eligible file and report whether that individual removal succeeded. Ask for confirmation once before the first deletion when the command is attached to a terminal; provide a `--yes` option for a scheduled noninteractive run. If deletion is requested without a terminal and without `--yes`, stop before deleting anything and explain how to proceed. A failed removal should be reported and must not prevent attempts on the remaining eligible files.

Use a readable, stable report format. Include the root, run-start time, retention period, and mode near the top. For each candidate considered, distinguish selected files from skipped files, and provide a concise reason for skips that are relevant to the administrator, such as a nonmatching filename, a future timestamp, or an unreadable modification time. Do not dump a traceback for an expected file-level problem. Keep paths unambiguous, including spaces and non-ASCII characters; do not shorten them in a way that could make two different paths look identical. Finish with counts for candidates, selected files, removed files, and file-level warnings. If an argument or root-level error prevents a run, return a nonzero exit status; if individual files fail but the scan completes, report those failures and use a nonzero status as well.

Please include a short explanation of the command-line options and the age rule, then provide the implementation and a practical test suite. The tests should use temporary directories and controlled timestamps rather than depend on the machine’s real log files or current time. Cover nested directories, both supported suffix forms, case variation, symbolic links, a valid dated name, an invalid calendar date, an undated name that falls back to modification time, a missing or unreadable timestamp where practical, and the exact-threshold boundary. Also test dry-run behavior to show that it leaves files untouched, and deletion behavior with confirmation handled safely in an automated test. Keep tests isolated so they cannot delete files outside their temporary directory.

I want the interface to stay modest: one required root directory, one required retention period, and only the options discussed above unless an implementation detail genuinely needs another setting. Use the language and standard-library approach you judge appropriate, but explain any dependency before relying on it. Structure the code so the filename-date decision, age comparison, and deletion step can be tested separately. Include a brief example of a dry run and a deletion invocation, using a fictional directory and values rather than assuming a particular server layout. Do not claim that the utility has been run against production logs; give me something I can review and test locally before scheduling it.
